miniProject.title: Evaluation and arithmetic dossier
miniProject.brief: Evaluate the trained model honestly and account for its cost. The evaluation is versioned and rerunnable, every number carries uncertainty, one evaluator failure is exposed on purpose, and every parameter, FLOP and memory estimate is reconciled with a measurement.
steps: Report validation likelihood and perplexity with the tokenizer and split named, and explain why the number does not compare across tokenizers.
Define one small task with a versioned prompt, parser and exact or structured metric, run it on your model, and store raw outputs next to the scores.
Report the metric on two slices with bootstrap intervals, and compare two checkpoints or decoding settings with a paired bootstrap.
Expose one evaluator failure on purpose, such as a parser that accepts a wrong format or a judge that prefers longer answers, and show the fix.
Run your section 1 contamination probe between the evaluation set and the training split, and report what it can and cannot rule out.
Write a worksheet of parameters, forward FLOPs, activation memory and AdamW memory for your model, and reconcile each with a measurement: FlopCounterMode, tensor sizes or peak memory.
Connect the atlas lab adapters for section 4 and pass tests/test_s4_eval_arithmetic.py.
deliverables: An evaluation manifest: data version, prompt, parser, metric, seeds and decoding config.
Raw outputs, slice scores with bootstrap intervals and the paired comparison.
The evaluator-failure case with results before and after the fix.
The arithmetic worksheet, with each estimate next to its measurement and the reason for any gap.

checks.name: Atlas lab, section 4: counts, memory and bootstrap intervals
checks.note: Run in labs/llm-foundations of an ai-atlas clone after you connect adapters.py to your package. It checks parameter and matmul-FLOP counts against exact counts of a reference module, AdamW memory, bootstrap determinism and coverage, and the paired bootstrap.

rubric.pass: Rerunning the manifest reproduces the scores.
rubric.strong: A changed prompt, parser or tokenizer changes the manifest hash, and the report says which changed.

rubric.pass: Every headline number has a bootstrap interval.
rubric.strong: The comparison uses a paired bootstrap, and the report states which claim the interval supports and which it does not.

rubric.pass: One failure is shown with its fix.
rubric.strong: You found the failure by reading raw outputs, and a regression test now covers it.

rubric.pass: The probe runs between evaluation and training data and its result is reported.
rubric.strong: The report separates overlap from memorization and lists what the probe cannot detect.

rubric.pass: The section 4 lab tests pass and every estimate is within 10 percent of its measurement.
rubric.strong: Every gap above 2 percent is explained, for example by elementwise ops, buffers or allocator overhead.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 3, the evaluation and arithmetic half of the dossier. Section 5 extends the memory worksheet with the KV cache.
